title: Metropolis Healthcare Ltd - 542650 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Metropolis guides 14-15% growth ex-price and ex-M&A, Q1 FY27 growth was 17%, and targets EBITDA margin of 27-28% from 24.4%.
summary.overview: Management held an investor and analyst meet (transcript dated 27 Aug 2026) covering strategy, growth levers, margin path and Q&A. Q1 growth was stated at 17%, ahead of the company's 14-15% medium-term guidance, which excludes price increases and acquisitions. Management outlined five growth engines: network expansion (collection-centre-to-lab ratio from 1:24 to 1:35), TruHealth, specialty and genomics, technology/digital, and inorganic growth. Radiology "mini hubs" (about 100 centres, 50 upgrades) were introduced as a new adjacency, with capex of about INR35-40 lakh per hub. Management said the FY26 EBITDA margin was 24.4% (25.9% organic, adjusted for the breakeven Core Diagnostics acquisition) and targeted 27-28% over the next 2-3 years.

financial_highlights.change: FY26 revenue CAGR 23.6% (as stated); 3-year revenue CAGR 17.6%
Core Diagnostics (breakeven at acquisition) diluted margin by about 1.5 pts
Above 14-15% guidance; B2C grew about 18% in the last quarter
B2B grew about 15% in the last quarter, aided by Core test menu
Added about 380-400 specialty tests in the last 15 months
Home collection contribution growing about 40% per quarter (as stated)
North India fastest-growing region in Q1; North could reach about 25% in a few years
Five countries, about 24 labs; Kenya and Zambia market leaders

segments.name: B2C
segments.commentary: About 57-59% of revenue; grew about 18% in the last quarter. Centre network of about 5,000 (about 700-800 company-owned, rest franchise); plan to add 250-300 centres every quarter and reach a 1:35 centre-to-lab ratio from 1:24.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: About 41-43% of revenue; grew about 15% last quarter, helped by Core Diagnostics' oncology test menu (about 350 tests, about 2,000 connected oncologists). Management targets B2B at about 45% with margin-accretive accounts only.

segments.name: Specialty and genomics
segments.commentary: About 40-42% of business; genomics volume reportedly doubled in the last year. Company claims a 2-CAP-accredited genomics labs footprint (West and North) and a clinician support vertical.

segments.name: TruHealth
segments.commentary: About 18-20% of revenue; target 25%. Adding diet consultation (blood-work based), body composition/vital check-up, and obesity/diabetes panels.

segments.name: Radiology mini hubs (new)
segments.commentary: Plan for about 100 hubs over the next couple of years (about 50 upgrades of existing centres, about 15-50 new per management, as stated); capex about INR35-40 lakh per hub for basic X-ray, ultrasound, echo, treadmill, with pilots of 50 centres in year 1. Advanced MRI/CT limited to 1-2 preventive-care pilots.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Five countries (Kenya, Zambia, Ghana, Uganda, Tanzania), about 24 labs; Kenya and Zambia rated market leaders, others top-3. Self-funded, with no capital sent from India.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term growth guidance reiterated at 14-15%, excluding price increases and acquisitions; management expects FY27 growth to run faster given Q1 at 17%, but is holding 14-15% until more clarity by end of year.
EBITDA margin ambition of 27-28% (from 24.4%) over the next 2-3 years, driven by specialty/genomics mix, digitisation and automation, and higher centre-to-lab utilisation.
Working capital aspiration to move from double-digit days to single digit; focus on ROCE and capital-light expansion.
Price increases not in guidance; management said it will give clarity on FY28 and pricing once the year ends.
Management described 2026-2029 as a period to harvest investments made in 2021-2025; further reinvestment expected in future cycles.
capex_capacity: Network: about 5,000 centres (about 700-800 company-owned, concentrated in top 6-8 towns); 209 labs; 750 towns served; plan to raise centre-to-lab ratio from 1:24 to 1:35.
Radiology mini hubs: about 100 over the next couple of years (about 50 upgrades of existing centres); capex about INR35-40 lakh per hub; first 50 centres in year 1, next 50 in about a year after.
Opex-versus-capex model under evaluation for mini hubs; corporate health checks and insurance to lift productivity 2-3x per centre (as stated).
Company-owned centres' real estate could be used beyond 10:30-11 AM for allied services; management said one lab need not be paired with one radiology centre.
Tier 3 labs already in place across 750 towns; no new labs needed, only more collection centres (250-300 added per quarter).
demand_pricing: Management attributes most growth to volume; price increases of 2-3% p.a. in prior years, plus product-mix-driven revenue per patient gains.
CGHS rate hike benefited peers in last year's Q3; Metropolis says it had negligible CGHS exposure, so it does not face a fade from Q3 onwards.
Semi-specialty and specialty tests carry the same price across India, while routine tests vary by market; Tier 3 margins said to be equal or better than metros.
Large-city share (Mumbai, Chennai, Pune) said to be stable or improving despite competition from health-tech players and pharma entrants.
Management criticised private players buying businesses at 18-19x EBITDA multiples and said it will remain disciplined on M&A pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What are the KRAs and KPIs for the top management team, given the 'professionally run, promoter-led' framing?
qa_highlights.answer: Ameera Shah said management goals fall into three buckets: current-year AOP and margin delivery, longer-term strategic projects with year-wise milestones, and a rotating focus area (e.g., controls and governance, or people and culture) depending on the year.

qa_highlights.question: What long-term operating margin should be expected given gross margins of about 78-80%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ameera Shah said operating leverage can keep building margins, but reinvestment cycles recur every few years (e.g., 100 more labs or new equipment). 2026-2029 is the harvest period after 2021-2025 investments. She said she would be happy with a steady-state margin close to current levels while reinvesting for growth; no numeric long-term margin was given.

qa_highlights.question: What capex and revenue contribution should be expected from radiology mini hubs over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Surendran Chemmenkotil said capex is about INR35-40 lakh per hub for X-ray, ultrasound, 2D echo, treadmill and sometimes DEXA, and the model is being evaluated as capex or opex. Productivity could rise 2-3x with corporate health checks. First 50 centres in year 1, next 50 about a year later. No revenue figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: How should FY28 be viewed given FY27 guidance, a possible price hike and radiology?
qa_highlights.answer: Surendran said guidance stays at 14-15% excluding price increases for the next 3-4 quarters; clarity on FY28 and pricing will come by year-end or 1-2 quarters later. He expects growth acceleration to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How does management view M&A consolidation and the pricing of assets, and will future deals resemble Chennai or smaller towns?
qa_highlights.answer: Ameera Shah said Metropolis will not pay 18-19x EBITDA multiples seen with private players, since pathology lacks pharma-style synergies. Likely targets are sub-scale businesses built over 10 years that can be turned around, preferably in markets where Metropolis is not present, or in existing markets if IRR is good.

qa_highlights.question: Is radiology a standalone strategy or linked to the government budget mandate for employee health checks over age 45? Is the network-centre revenue B2B or B2C?
qa_highlights.answer: Surendran said network centres are purely B2C walk-in, with only 2-5% possibly coming via B2B-to-customer tie-ups in smaller towns. Mini hubs are a serious strategy targeting top 5-6 towns; B2C:B2B is 59:41 currently, with management aiming for about 60:40 with B2C grown faster.

qa_highlights.question: Does Tier 3 carry lower margins, and how does the test mix evolve beyond Tier 2?
qa_highlights.answer: Ameera Shah said Tier 3 mix is mainly semi-specialty and specialty rather than routine, with specialty tests priced uniformly across India, so Tier 3 margins are equal or better than metros. Mohan Menon described a hub-and-spoke model with regional reference labs and Mumbai as global reference lab.

risks_watch: Medium-term 14-15% guidance ex-price and ex-M&A is held despite 17% Q1; sustainability of the 17% print and the timing of FY28 pricing clarity by year-end.
Margin ramp to 27-28% from 24.4% depends on centre-to-lab ratio (1:24 to 1:35), specialty mix, and utilisation of 700-800 owned centres; no quarterly margin path given.
Radiology mini hub economics unproven: capex model vs opex still under evaluation, no revenue target, and pilots of 50 centres in year 1.
Working capital still in double-digit days with an aspiration to single digit; automation timelines not specified.
Acquisition discipline: management is refusing 18-19x EBITDA deals, which may limit inorganic growth, while core growth engines depend on M&A integration.
Competition from health-tech, pharma entrants and hospital chains in large cities; management says Mumbai, Chennai and Pune share is stable but gave no data.
International business (under 10% of revenue) is self-funded, with no quantified growth or margin disclosure.
key_quotes: So we will experiment with first maybe 50 centers in year 1.
So, our aspiration is to take our working capital to a single digit from currently the double-digit working capital.

Then definitely this is without any price increase and also, please remember, I mean, we didn't have any benefit of the CGHS price increase because our CGHS business was very low and almost negligible, you know, earlier.
In pathology, the price you pay is a very critical piece of it.
'26 to '29 is really the period for us to reap the fruit of all of this, right?
summary.management_tone: Confident and long-horizon on structural growth, specialty, and M&A discipline, with a clear 2026-2029 harvest framing. Cautious and non-committal on pricing, FY28 guidance, radiology revenue and long-term margins, deferring details to year-end.

Collection centres: plan to add 250-300 centres every quarter (about 5,000 network) to lift centre-to-lab ratio from 1:24 to 1:35

growth.why: Management reiterates 14-15% medium-term growth ex-price and M&A, with Q1 FY27 at 17%, and is adding 250-300 collection centres per quarter plus about 100 radiology mini hubs; the guidance excludes price, so the outlook leans positive but is not formally raised.
